e-4397.knowledge_point: Multiplying a 2x2 Matrix by a Column Vector
e-4397.worked_solution:
We multiply each row in the matrix by the column vector using the dot product. Multiplying the first row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 7 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1\cdot 2+3\cdot 5 \\ ∗\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}17 \\ ∗\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying the second row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 7 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}17 \\ 7\cdot 2+(-2)\cdot 5\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}17 \\ 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

e-4398.knowledge_point: Multiplying a 3x3 Matrix by a Column Vector
e-4398.worked_solution:
We multiply each row in the matrix by the column vector using the dot product:

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(-3)\cdot 1+1\cdot (-2)+1\cdot 0 \\ 2\cdot 1+0\cdot (-2)+0\cdot 0 \\ (-1)\cdot 1+(-2)\cdot (-2)+5\cdot 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3-2+0 \\ 2+0+0 \\ -1+4+0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

e-4399.knowledge_point: Multiplying a Matrix With Variable Entries by a Column Vector
e-4399.worked_solution:
We multiply each row in the matrix by the column vector using the dot product:

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax & =[\begin{aligned}a & c \\ b & d\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}a\cdot 3+c\cdot 2 \\ b\cdot 3+d\cdot 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3a+2c \\ 3b+2d\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Multiplying a 2x2 Matrix by a Column Vector
content.worked_solution:
We multiply each row in the matrix by the column vector using the dot product. Multiplying the first row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 2 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3\cdot 2+4\cdot 2 \\ ∗\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}14 \\ ∗\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying the second row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 2 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}14 \\ 2\cdot 2+6\cdot 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}14 \\ 16\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 2 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}14 \\ 16\end{aligned}].
$$

decision.explanation: The row dot products are (-7)(-3)+2(2)=25 and 2(-3)+(-5)(2)=-16, so option a is correct.

after.name: Question 5
after.worked_solution:
We multiply each row in the matrix by the column vector using the dot product. Multiplying the first row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}-7 & 2 \\ 2 & -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}(-7)\cdot -3+2\cdot 2 \\ ∗\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}25 \\ ∗\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying the second row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}-7 & 2 \\ 2 & -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}25 \\ 2\cdot -3+(-5)\cdot 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}25 \\ -16\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 
$Hn=[\begin{aligned}25 \\ -16\end{aligned}].$

content.knowledge_point: Multiplying a 2x2 Matrix by a Column Vector
content.worked_solution:
We multiply each row in the matrix by the column vector using the dot product. Multiplying the first row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}-7 & 2 \\ 2 & -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}(-7)\cdot -3+2\cdot 2 \\ ∗\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}25 \\ ∗\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying the second row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}-7 & 2 \\ 2 & -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}25 \\ 2\cdot -3+(-5)\cdot 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}25 \\ -16\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 
$Hn=[\begin{aligned}25 \\ -16\end{aligned}].$

after.name: Question 6
after.worked_solution:
We multiply each row in the matrix by the column vector using the dot product:

$$

decision.explanation: The row dot products are -2+2+3=3, 4-2-6=-4, and -2+2+3=3. Thus option c is correct.

after.name: Question 7
after.worked_solution:
We multiply each row in the matrix by the column vector using the dot product:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ -2 & 2 & -2 \\ 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1\cdot (-2)+(-2)\cdot (-1)+1\cdot 3 \\ (-2)\cdot (-2)+2\cdot (-1)+(-2)\cdot 3 \\ 1\cdot (-2)+(-2)\cdot (-1)+1\cdot 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2+2+3 \\ 4-2-6 \\ -2+2+3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Multiplying a 3x3 Matrix by a Column Vector
content.worked_solution:
We multiply each row in the matrix by the column vector using the dot product:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}6 & -4 & -6 \\ -2 & 5 & 2 \\ -1 & -4 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}6\cdot 2+(-4)\cdot (-1)+(-6)\cdot 2 \\ (-2)\cdot 2+5\cdot (-1)+2\cdot 2 \\ (-1)\cdot 2+(-4)\cdot (-1)+1\cdot 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}12+4-12 \\ -4-5+4 \\ -2+4+2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -5 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: The row dot products are 0-4-2=-6, 0-4-3=-7, and 0-4-4=-8. Thus option d is correct.

after.name: Question 9
after.worked_solution:
We multiply each row in the matrix by the column vector using the dot product:

$$
\begin{aligned}Pv & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & 3 \\ 1 & -1 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1\cdot 0+(-1)\cdot 4+2\cdot (-1) \\ 1\cdot 0+(-1)\cdot 4+3\cdot (-1) \\ 1\cdot 0+(-1)\cdot 4+4\cdot (-1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0-4-2 \\ 0-4-3 \\ 0-4-4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -7 \\ -8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Multiplying a 3x3 Matrix by a Column Vector
content.worked_solution:
We multiply each row in the matrix by the column vector using the dot product:

$$
\begin{aligned}Pv & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & 3 \\ 1 & -1 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1\cdot 0+(-1)\cdot 4+2\cdot (-1) \\ 1\cdot 0+(-1)\cdot 4+3\cdot (-1) \\ 1\cdot 0+(-1)\cdot 4+4\cdot (-1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0-4-2 \\ 0-4-3 \\ 0-4-4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -7 \\ -8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

provenance.kp_title: Multiplying a 3x3 Matrix by a Column Vector

history.worked_solution:
We multiply each row in the matrix by the column vector using the dot product:

$$
\begin{aligned}Pv & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & 3 \\ 1 & -1 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1\cdot 0+(-1)\cdot 4+2\cdot (-1) \\ 1\cdot 0+(-1)\cdot 4+3\cdot (-1) \\ 1\cdot 0+(-1)\cdot 4+4\cdot (-1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0-4-2 \\ 0-4-3 \\ 0-4-4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -7 \\ -8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: The row dot products are 12-3+1=10, -18-6-1=-25, and 24+0-3=21. Thus option d is correct.

after.name: Question 10
after.worked_solution:
We multiply each row in the matrix by the column vector using the dot product:

$$
\begin{aligned}By & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 1 \\ -3 & 2 & -1 \\ 4 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}6 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2\cdot 6+1\cdot (-3)+1\cdot 1 \\ (-3)\cdot 6+2\cdot (-3)+(-1)\cdot 1 \\ 4\cdot 6+0\cdot (-3)+(-3)\cdot 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}12-3+1 \\ -18-6-1 \\ 24-0-3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -25 \\ 21\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}By & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 1 \\ -3 & 2 & -1 \\ 4 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}6 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2\cdot 6+1\cdot (-3)+1\cdot 1 \\ (-3)\cdot 6+2\cdot (-3)+(-1)\cdot 1 \\ 4\cdot 6+0\cdot (-3)+(-3)\cdot 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}12-3+1 \\ -18-6-1 \\ 24-0-3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -25 \\ 21\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 13
?

Find Mz if M=[st−ts] and z=[st].

a
[s2+t20]
b
[s2+t2−2st]
c
[(s+t)2−2st]
d
[(s−t)20]
e
[(s+t)20]
Submit

decision.explanation: The row dot products are s·s+t·t=s²+t² and (-t)s+st=0. Thus option a is correct.

after.name: Question 13
after.problem:
Find $Mz$ if 
$M=[\begin{aligned}s & t \\ -t & s\end{aligned}]$
and
$z=[\begin{aligned}s \\ t\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
We multiply each row in the matrix by the column vector using the dot product:

$$
\begin{aligned}Mz & =[\begin{aligned}s & t \\ -t & s\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}s \\ t\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}s\cdot s+t\cdot t \\ (-t)\cdot s+s\cdot t\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{s}^{2}+{t}^{2} \\ -st+st\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{s}^{2}+{t}^{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Multiplying a Matrix With Variable Entries by a Column Vector
content.problem:
Find $Mz$ if 
$M=[\begin{aligned}s & t \\ -t & s\end{aligned}]$
and
$z=[\begin{aligned}s \\ t\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
We multiply each row in the matrix by the column vector using the dot product:

$$
\begin{aligned}Mz & =[\begin{aligned}s & t \\ -t & s\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}s \\ t\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}s\cdot s+t\cdot t \\ (-t)\cdot s+s\cdot t\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{s}^{2}+{t}^{2} \\ -st+st\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{s}^{2}+{t}^{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 15
?

Find Tu if T=[xyxx−yx−x−yx] and u=[x0−x].

a
[x3y0−x3y]
b
[x2−x20]
c
[x20−x2]
d
[x2y0−x2y]
e
[00−2x2]
Submit

decision.explanation: The row dot products are x²+0-x²=0, x²+0-x²=0, and -x²+0-x²=-2x². Thus option e is correct.

after.name: Question 15
after.problem:
Find $Tu$ if 
$T=[\begin{aligned}x & y & x \\ x & -y & x \\ -x & -y & x\end{aligned}]$
and
$u=[\begin{aligned}x \\ 0 \\ -x\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
We multiply each row in the matrix by the column vector using the dot product:

$$
\begin{aligned}Tu & =[\begin{aligned}x & y & x \\ x & -y & x \\ -x & -y & x\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ 0 \\ -x\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}x\cdot x+y\cdot 0+x\cdot (-x) \\ x\cdot x+(-y)\cdot 0+x\cdot (-x) \\ (-x)\cdot x+(-y)\cdot 0+x\cdot (-x)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+0-{x}^{2} \\ {x}^{2}+0-{x}^{2} \\ -{x}^{2}+0-{x}^{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ -2{x}^{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

We multiply each row in the matrix by the column vector using the dot product:

Tu=[xyxx−yx−x−yx][x0−x]=[x⋅x+y⋅0+x⋅(−x)x⋅x+(−y)⋅0+x⋅(−x)(−x)⋅x+(−y)⋅0+x⋅(−x)]=[x2+0−x2x2+0−x2−x2+0−x2]=[00−2x2]

content.knowledge_point: Multiplying a Matrix With Variable Entries by a Column Vector
content.problem:
Find $Tu$ if 
$T=[\begin{aligned}x & y & x \\ x & -y & x \\ -x & -y & x\end{aligned}]$
and
$u=[\begin{aligned}x \\ 0 \\ -x\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
We multiply each row in the matrix by the column vector using the dot product:

$$
\begin{aligned}Tu & =[\begin{aligned}x & y & x \\ x & -y & x \\ -x & -y & x\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ 0 \\ -x\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}x\cdot x+y\cdot 0+x\cdot (-x) \\ x\cdot x+(-y)\cdot 0+x\cdot (-x) \\ (-x)\cdot x+(-y)\cdot 0+x\cdot (-x)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+0-{x}^{2} \\ {x}^{2}+0-{x}^{2} \\ -{x}^{2}+0-{x}^{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ -2{x}^{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
